Benchmarks

benchmarks.Rmd

CPU Benchmarks

Speedup relative to R’s stats::lowess (higher is better):

Category R baseline rfastlowess Serial rfastlowess Parallel
Clustered 1.88 ms 0.8× 2.1×
Constant Y 1.50 ms 0.7× 2.0×
Extreme Outliers 5.32 ms 0.9× 2.0×
Financial (500–5K) 0.60 ms 1.0× 1.3×
Fraction (0.05–0.67) 3.24 ms 0.9× 2.4×
Genomic (1K–100K) 8.50 ms 1.0× 1.9×
High Noise 6.98 ms 0.9× 3.0×
Iterations (0–10) 2.28 ms 0.8× 1.7×
Large (50K, delta=0) 10.16 s 1.6× 7.3×
Large (50K, delta=auto) 11.48 ms 0.8× 2.0×
Large (50K, 10 iter) 37.17 s 2.7× 9.8×
Large (20K, fraction=0.67) 10.90 s 2.3× 12.2×
Scale (1K–10K) 1.36 ms 1.0× 1.4×
Scientific (500–5K) 0.87 ms 1.3× 1.4×

Times are averages of the per-scenario medians in multi-scenario categories; speedups are averages of the corresponding per-scenario speedups. Individual scenario results are in the benchmarks README.

GPU Backend

For large batch datasets, the GPU backend can outperform CPU-parallel execution. The crossover point depends on fraction × n:

Fraction Iterations = 0 Iterations = 3
0.1 n ≥ 100K n ≥ 250K
0.3 n ≥ 100K n ≥ 100K
0.5 n ≥ 50K n ≥ 50K

The table gives the first dataset size where GPU median time is less than CPU-parallel median time. A representative large-data result is:

Scenario CPU-Parallel GPU Speedup
n = 1M, fraction = 0.5 1.24 s 187 ms 6.6×

See the benchmarks README in the source repository for the full sweep, end-to-end GPU timings, and transfer-overhead breakdown.
